about: The labs, in the recommended order. Each lab is one subject: Learn (short pages in our own words, each with passages from Microsoft Learn through the concepts it names, and a quiz), Do (tasks in the simulated environment, checked by code; {placeholders} are filled from the environment, src/labs/labs.ts), and Challenge (ready-made exercises, ids from content/scenarios/ready-made.json). A planned lab is listed so learners see the whole path.

labs.title: How a call finds its way
labs.summary: What Contact Center does, and the path a call takes from phone number to representative.

learn.title: What Contact Center does
text: Dynamics 365 Contact Center lets a company answer its customers on channels like chat, messaging and voice. This training is about voice: customers phone a number, and a representative helps them.

Between the ringing phone and the representative, unified routing decides where the call goes and who takes it. It first adds information to the call, then sends it to a queue and assigns it to a person who is free.

learn.title: The path of a call
text: Every call follows the same path. The phone number belongs to a voice channel. The voice channel belongs to a workstream: the workstream takes the call in and decides where it goes.
Many workstreams have an AI agent that answers first, like an IVR menu. Then the workstream's route-to-queue rules pick a queue, and the queue's assignment method picks a representative.

learn.title: The caller's answer
text: When an AI agent asks “What is your call about?”, the caller's answer is kept on the call in a context variable, for example SelectedMenuItem = Billing.
Routing rules can read that value. That's how a choice in the menu leads to a queue.

learn.title: Queues and the safety net
text: A queue holds calls until a representative takes them. Only the members of a queue get its calls.
A call that no route-to-queue rule picks up isn't lost: it goes to the workstream's fallback queue. That keeps the call, but the people there may not be the right ones.

learn.title: Where you work in this training
text: Admin center: a simulation of the Copilot Service admin center, where you set things up. It has Microsoft's menu and field names, with our own look.
Diagram: how everything connects, from phone numbers to people. Phone: call any number and follow the call step by step. Agent: be a representative or a supervisor in the workspace.
Nothing here is real: the environment, the people and the phone numbers are made up, so you can change anything.

quiz.question: What decides which queue a call goes to?
options: The phone number on its own
The language of the voice channel
quiz.why: The workstream's route-to-queue rules pick the queue. The phone number only decides which workstream takes the call.

quiz.question: A call matches none of the route-to-queue rules. Where does it go?
options: To the first queue in the list
quiz.why: The fallback queue is the safety net for calls no rule picks up.

quiz.question: Where does the caller's answer to the IVR end up?
options: In a context variable on the call
In the name of the queue
quiz.why: The AI agent stores the answer in a context variable, and routing rules can check it.

labs.title: Phone numbers and the voice channel
labs.summary: Where calls come in: numbers, voice channels, and which workstream answers.

learn.title: Phone numbers
text: Customers reach the contact center on phone numbers. An administrator gets numbers with calling plans: to receive calls, to make them, or both.
In this training the numbers are simulated and come from ranges kept for films and TV, so they never ring a real phone.

learn.title: The voice channel
text: A number does nothing until it's on a voice channel. The voice channel connects the number to a voice workstream and holds settings like language and hold music.
One workstream can answer several numbers, for example a main number and a second line.

learn.title: Which workstream answers
text: The workstream behind the number decides everything that follows: whether an IVR answers, which rules route the call, and which fallback queue catches the rest.
So the first question for any call is: which workstream answers this number?

learn.title: Numbers in the admin center
text: Numbers are under Channels, then Phone numbers. There you can get a new number and set up the workstream that answers it.
A workstream's page shows its voice channel and its numbers.

quiz.question: A new number has calling plans but isn't on a voice channel. What happens when a customer calls it?
options: It rings in the fallback queue
Nobody answers: no workstream takes the call
quiz.why: Only a voice channel connects a number to a workstream.

quiz.question: Can one workstream answer more than one phone number?
options: Yes, for example a main number and a second line
quiz.why: A workstream can have several numbers, each on its voice channel.

quiz.question: Which calling plan does a number need so customers can call in?
quiz.why: Receiving calls needs the plan to receive; making calls is a separate plan.

labs.title: Workstreams
labs.summary: What a workstream does with a call: its fallback queue and how it distributes work.

learn.title: What a workstream does
text: A workstream takes in work from its channels and decides where it goes. For voice: it answers the numbers on its voice channel, lets an AI agent ask questions first, routes the call to a queue and decides how the work is handed out.

learn.title: The AI agent
text: A workstream can have an AI agent that answers every call first, like an IVR menu. Its answers become context variables on the call. Without an AI agent the call goes straight to routing.

learn.title: The fallback queue
text: Every workstream has a fallback queue. Calls that no route-to-queue rule picks up go there.
Choose it with care: it should be a queue with people who can at least help the caller on.

learn.title: Work distribution
text: The workstream also says how work is handed out: which capacity profile its calls use, and in which presences representatives can get them.
In this training's voice workstreams, calls use the profile Default voice inbound, and representatives who are Available or Busy can get them.

quiz.question: A voice workstream has no AI agent. What happens to its calls?
options: They go straight to the route-to-queue rules
They wait for an AI agent
quiz.why: Without an AI agent nothing asks the caller first; routing starts straight away.

quiz.question: Which calls end up in a workstream's fallback queue?
options: Calls that no route-to-queue rule picks up
quiz.why: The fallback queue is the safety net for calls no rule routes.

quiz.question: Where does a workstream say which capacity profile its calls use?
quiz.why: Work distribution holds the capacity profile and the allowed presences.

labs.title: Queues and representatives
labs.summary: Queues, who is in them, and what a representative needs to get a call: presence and capacity.

learn.title: Queues
text: A queue holds calls until a representative takes them. Each queue is for one kind of work; calls need a voice queue.
You create queues in the admin center under Queues, then Advanced queues.

learn.title: Who is in a queue
text: Representatives are the people who take calls. You add them to a queue as its users.
Only members of a queue get its calls. A queue without members holds calls that nobody can answer.

learn.title: Presence
text: Presence says whether a representative can take work right now: Available, Busy, Away, Do not disturb or Offline (in this training Do not disturb is called Busy - DND). A representative sets it at the top of the workspace.

Each workstream lists the presences it assigns work to. In this training's workstreams that's Available and Busy. In the product, presence also changes by itself as a representative's capacity fills up; the training doesn't do that.

learn.title: Capacity
text: A capacity profile says how much work a representative can take at the same time, for example one call.
After a call ends, the representative is in wrap-up. Their capacity stays in use until they close the session, so they don't get a new call in the middle of their notes.

learn.title: Who gets the call
text: When a call waits in a queue, the queue's assignment method picks one of the members who can take it: in an allowed presence, with capacity left.
Least active is the default for voice queues: the call goes to the member who has been least active.

quiz.question: Mia is Available, but she isn't a member of the Billing queue. Can routing give her a Billing call?
options: No: only members of a queue get its calls
Only if she has the right skill
quiz.why: Assignment only looks at the queue's own members.

quiz.question: Which representatives can get calls from this training's voice workstreams?
options: Those who are Available or Busy, with capacity left
Anyone who is signed in, whatever their presence
quiz.why: The workstream's allowed presences are Available and Busy, and the representative needs capacity left.

quiz.question: A representative selected End. When is their capacity free for the next call?
options: When they close the session after wrap-up
quiz.why: In wrap-up the capacity stays in use until the session is closed.

labs.title: Assignment and capacity
labs.summary: How a queue picks a representative: assignment methods and capacity profiles.

learn.title: Who gets the call
text: When a call waits in a queue, the queue's assignment method picks one of its members. Only members who can take it count: in an allowed presence, with capacity left.

learn.title: The methods
text: Least active, the default for voice queues: the member who has been least active gets the call.
Highest capacity: the member with the most free capacity. Advanced round robin: members take turns in a fixed order.
No auto assignment: nobody gets calls automatically; representatives pick them up.

learn.title: Capacity profiles
text: A capacity profile says how much work of a kind a representative can take at the same time. With a work item limit of 1, a representative takes one call at a time.
Raise the limit and they can have a second call, for example one on hold.

learn.title: Putting them together
text: Presence decides who can work now, capacity decides how much, and the assignment method decides who goes first.
When nobody qualifies, the call waits in the queue and routing keeps trying.

quiz.question: Which assignment method does a new voice queue get?
quiz.why: Least active is the default selection for voice and messaging queues.

quiz.question: A representative's voice profile has a work item limit of 1 and they're on a call. Can they get a second call?
options: No, not until they close the first one
quiz.why: The limit is reached until the first call's session is closed.

quiz.question: Every member of a queue is Away. What happens to a new call?
options: It goes to the fallback queue
It waits in the queue, and routing keeps trying
quiz.why: The call stays in its queue until someone can take it.

labs.title: The IVR and context variables
labs.summary: What the AI agent asks, and how the answer becomes something routing can use.

learn.title: The AI agent answers first
text: On a workstream with an AI agent, every call is answered by the agent first. As an IVR it asks the caller what the call is about.

learn.title: Context variables
text: The agent keeps the caller's answers on the call as context variables, for example SelectedMenuItem = Billing. A workstream lists the context variables its calls can have.
Routing rules read them; the representative sees them too, on the Active Conversation form.

learn.title: Values must match
text: A rule compares the variable with a value. The value has to be exactly what the agent sends: if the agent sends Billing and the rule checks Invoices, the rule never matches.
When a caller says something no rule checks, the call goes to the fallback queue.

learn.title: Lines without an IVR
text: Not every line has an AI agent. On such a line nobody asks the caller anything, so no menu choice reaches routing.

quiz.question: Where does the caller's menu choice end up?
options: In a context variable on the call
quiz.why: The AI agent stores answers in context variables.

quiz.question: A line has no AI agent. Can a rule on SelectedMenuItem route its calls?
options: No: nobody asked, so the variable has no value
quiz.why: Without an IVR the caller isn't asked, so there's nothing to compare.

quiz.question: A caller says something no rule checks. Where does the call go?
options: To the first queue in the list
quiz.why: Calls no rule picks up go to the fallback queue.

labs.title: Route-to-queue rules
labs.summary: Rules that send a call to a queue: conditions, order, hit policy and the fallback queue.

learn.title: From an answer to a queue
text: The IVR keeps the caller's answer in a context variable. The workstream's route-to-queue ruleset holds rules that read it.
Each rule says: if this is true about the call, send it to that queue.

learn.title: Writing a rule
text: Open the workstream, then its ruleset under Route to queues, and select Create rule. Give the rule a name, add a condition, and pick the queue.
A condition compares a field with a value, for example SelectedMenuItem Equals Billing. The value must be exactly what the IVR sends; “Billing invoice” doesn't match “Billing”.

learn.title: When more than one rule matches
text: The rules are a decision list, in order. When several rules match and no queue is overflowing, the first rule in the list wins.
The rule hit policy says what happens when a queue is overflowing: Hit-all moves on to the next matching rule; Hit-first stays with the first one.

learn.title: When no rule matches
text: A call that no rule picks up goes to the workstream's fallback queue. A new menu choice without a rule always ends there.
So when calls pile up in the fallback queue, look for a choice that has no rule, or a rule whose value doesn't match.

learn.title: Sharing calls between queues
text: One rule can share its calls between up to five queues, with a percentage for each that adds up to 100, for example 70% to one team and 30% to another.

quiz.question: The IVR sends “Billing”. Your rule checks SelectedMenuItem Equals “Billing invoice”. What happens to the call?
options: The rule doesn't match, so another rule or the fallback queue takes the call
quiz.why: The value has to match what the IVR sends.

quiz.question: Two rules match a call, and neither queue is overflowing. Which queue does the call go to?
options: The queue of the first rule in the decision list
The queue of the last rule
The queue with the most members
quiz.why: Learn: the system selects the queue of the first rule in the list.

quiz.question: Where do you add a route-to-queue rule?
options: On the workstream, in its route-to-queue ruleset
quiz.why: Routing rules belong to the workstream.

labs.title: Work classification and skills
labs.summary: Adding information to a call before routing: Priority Score, skills and skill-based routing.

learn.title: Before routing: classification
text: Unified routing first classifies a call: rules add information to it. Only then do the route-to-queue rules run, and they can use what was added.

learn.title: Work classification rulesets
text: A workstream can have up to ten work classification rulesets. They run in order. In each, the first rule that matches sets its output, for example Priority Score = 10.
You find them on the workstream, under Work classification.

learn.title: Skills
text: Skills, such as a language or a product, describe what a representative knows, at a proficiency like Beginner, Intermediate or Expert.
A skill attachment rule adds a skill to a call, for example Technical when the caller picks Technical.

learn.title: Skill matching
text: The workstream's Default skill matching algorithm decides how skills count. Exact Match only gives the call to someone with every needed skill at the needed level; Closest Match gives it to whoever comes closest.
With Exact Match and nobody qualified, the call stays in the queue.

quiz.question: What runs first for an incoming call?
quiz.why: Classification runs before routing, so the rules can use what it added.

quiz.question: Two rules in one classification ruleset match a call. Which output is set?
quiz.why: In each ruleset, the first rule that matches sets its output.

quiz.question: With Exact Match, nobody in the queue has the needed skill. What happens?
options: The call stays unassigned in the queue
The call goes to the fallback queue
quiz.why: Exact Match waits for someone with every needed skill.

labs.title: Operating hours and overflow
labs.summary: Calls out of hours and when queues are full: voicemail, callback and transfers.

learn.title: Operating hours
text: Operating hours say when a queue is open, for example weekdays 9 to 5. They're set on the queue.
A queue without operating hours is always open, even when nobody is at work.

learn.title: Overflow
text: Overflow handling says what happens when a queue is closed or too busy. It's set on the queue too.
Before a call is queued, conditions like Out of operation hours or a long estimated wait can send it elsewhere: voicemail, a callback, the end of the call, or another queue.

learn.title: Testing with the clock
text: The training has its own clock. On the Phone tab, When lets you call on another day and time, to see what happens out of hours.
A call at another time only shows where it would go; it isn't given to anyone.

quiz.question: A queue has no operating hours. When is it open?
quiz.why: Without operating hours a queue counts as open all the time.

quiz.question: Where do you set what happens to calls out of hours?
quiz.why: Overflow handling is a setting of the queue.

quiz.question: Which condition sends callers elsewhere when the wait is predicted to be long?
quiz.why: A long predicted wait is an overflow condition before the call is queued.

labs.title: The workspace
labs.summary: The representative's and supervisor's side: sessions, transcript, Copilot, monitoring and real-time analytics.

learn.title: The representative's workspace
text: Representatives work in the Copilot Service workspace. They set their presence at the top, get a notification for each call, and work each call in its own session tab.
The Agent tab in this training is a simulation of it.

learn.title: Who is calling
text: When the caller's number matches one contact's mobile phone or one account's phone, the call is linked to that customer. The representative sees their details and earlier conversations.
When the number matches more than one record, nothing is linked and the representative searches for the customer.

learn.title: During the call
text: The call controls are in the Communication Panel: Mute, Hold, Consult, Transfer and End. The live transcript shows what is said.
After End, the call is in wrap-up until the representative closes the session.

learn.title: Copilot
text: Copilot summarizes the conversation when the representative selects Summarize conversation, and by itself on a consult, a transfer or the end of the call. In this training the summary is written from the call's data.

learn.title: The supervisor
text: Supervisors watch the contact center in Omnichannel real-time analytics: calls offered, how fast they're answered, who is available.
On ongoing conversations they can Monitor an active call without being seen, Join call when help is needed, and assign, transfer or end conversations.

quiz.question: A caller's number belongs to two contacts. What does the representative see?
options: No linked customer: they search for the customer
quiz.why: When more than one record matches, nothing is linked.

quiz.question: A representative selected End. What's left to do?
quiz.why: To end the call after End, the representative closes the session.

quiz.question: A supervisor monitors a call. Who knows?
options: Nobody, until the supervisor joins the call
quiz.why: Monitoring is silent; joining the call tells the representative.

do.finished: You've worked a call from both sides: as the representative and as the supervisor. One lab to go.

labs.title: Putting it together
labs.summary: Whole requests from a customer, from interview to a working line.

learn.title: The whole path
text: You've seen every part of a call's path: number, voice channel, workstream, AI agent, classification, route-to-queue rules, queue, overflow, assignment and the representative.
A real request touches several of them at once.

learn.title: From request to setup
text: Customers describe what they see, not settings. “Delivery questions should reach a small team in office hours” means: a queue, people in it, a rule for the menu choice, operating hours and overflow.
Ask questions until you know what they need, then build it, then test it with calls.

learn.title: Testing
text: Every change can be tested with the Phone tab: call with the right choice, at the right time, and read the trace.
The Diagram shows the whole setup at once, and marks problems.

quiz.question: “Delivery calls should reach a new team.” Which parts do you need?
options: A queue with people, and a rule for the Delivery choice
quiz.why: Without people nobody answers; without a rule the calls never reach the queue.

quiz.question: How do you check your setup works?
options: Call it on the Phone tab and read the trace
quiz.why: A test call shows each step the call takes.

quiz.question: The team works office hours only. What else do you set?
options: Operating hours and what happens out of hours
quiz.why: Hours on the queue, and overflow for out-of-hours callers.
